question.problem: The axis of symmetry of the parabola $y=-(x+6)(x-4)$ is $x=${{field-1}}.
question.worked_solution:
From the equation $y=-(x+6)(x-4),$ we can tell that the roots of the parabola are ${x}_{1}=-6$ and ${x}_{2}=4.$ 

To find the axis of symmetry, we take the average of the roots, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}x & =\frac{{x}_{1}+{x}_{2}}{2} \\  & =\frac{-6+4}{2} \\  & =\frac{(-2)}{2} \\  & =-1\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the axis of symmetry is $x=-1.$
